chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast on the Day of Arafah since the fasting of the month of Ramadan was revealed.'

key_terms.صِيَامُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet fast on the Day of Arafah after the revelation of Ramadan fasting?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s consistent practice of fasting on the Day of Arafah until the revelation of Ramadan’s obligatory fasting, after which he ceased it to avoid confusion or to emphasize the superiority of the month-long fast. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often discussed in the context of *naskh* (abrogation) or *tarjih* (preference), where the general obligation of Ramadan superseded the specific voluntary fast of Arafah for the Prophet, though it remains highly recommended for pilgrims and non-pilgrims alike. The hadith underscores the dynamic nature of prophetic practice in response to divine legislative changes.
